intervals.label: construction
intervals.note: Year precision. The end is the year the first electron beam was stored ('the end of 1967').
intervals.quote: The construction of the new machine began in 1963

intervals.label: first beams and commissioning
intervals.note: Year precision. The first positron injections met the 'head-tail' instability, cured by a feedback system. Bonolis & Pancheri: ADONE 'started functioning at the end of 1968 and began taking data in 1969'.
intervals.quote: The first electron beam was stored at the end of 1967.

intervals.label: e+e- collider operation
intervals.note: Start at year precision (the LNF history list dates the ADONE entry 17 November 1969, without saying what happened that day). End = shutdown. The ring ran as a collider 1969-1978 and 1990-1993 and as a single-beam source in between.
intervals.quote: The study of the physics of electron-positron collisions started in 1969 with the ADONE accelerator.

intervals.label: colliding-beam physics, first and second generation experiments
intervals.quote: The first generation experiments, and successively the second generation ones, explored the physics of electron-positron collisions up to 3.0 GeV in the center of mass, from 1969 to 1978.

intervals.label: single-beam operation (synchrotron radiation and gamma-ray beams)
intervals.note: Year precision. 'After that time [1978] the storage ring was deeply modified' to serve as a synchrotron-radiation source (PULS, PWA) and a gamma-ray source (LADON, Jet Target); two-beam operation resumed in 1990.
intervals.quote: In 1990, after several years dedicated to single beam operation for synchrotron radiation and nuclear physics, two beam operation with electrons and positrons was resumed to perform the last subnuclear physics experiment, FENICE, whose data taking lasted until the final shutdown of ADONE in 1993.

intervals.label: e+e- operation resumed for FENICE
intervals.note: Year precision for the start; the same page elsewhere says 'in 1991, electron-positron operation was resumed' (see the log). Data taking lasted until the final shutdown.
intervals.quote: In 1990, after several years dedicated to single beam operation for synchrotron radiation and nuclear physics, two beam operation with electrons and positrons was resumed to perform the last subnuclear physics experiment, FENICE, whose data taking lasted until the final shutdown of ADONE in 1993.

intervals.label: J/psi run beyond the standard parameters
intervals.note: Month precision from the November 1974 discovery and the PRL received 18 November 1974. The J/psi lies about 0.1 GeV above ADONE's nominal operating energy; the signal appeared 'after three days' (LNF page) or 'in two days' (Bernardini et al.).
intervals.quote: However, it was decided to push the performance of the machine beyond its standard parameters, in the energy range indicated by the american laboratories.

cms_energy.note: The page gives the new particle's mass as about 3.1 GeV and says the energy needed was only ~0.1 GeV above ADONE's nominal operating energy (3.0 GeV).
cms_energy.quote: characterised by an extraordinary stability for its large mass, ~3.1 GeV

intervals.label: ADONE shut down
intervals.note: After 24 years of operation (about 22000 hours of colliding beams and 5300 hours of single beams).
intervals.quote: ADONE was shut down on April 26, 1993 to allow the construction of a new low energy, high luminosity collider, DAFNE, inside its building

website.locator: INFN-LNF page title (The history of LNF)
website.note: A history page; ADONE no longer operates.

name: ADONE
notes: The sources fetched give both the design maximum (3.0 GeV centre-of-mass energy) and a brief push to about 3.1 GeV in November 1974 to study the J/psi; the headline value is the 3.0 GeV design maximum and the 1974 run is a dated phase (the energy-frontier chart then draws the headline as the energy 'as recorded today' at the start of operation).

After 1978 ADONE ran with single beams as a synchrotron-radiation source and a gamma-ray source; photon science is outside the Atlas scope (A26), so those phases are recorded only as dates. Collider running resumed in 1990-1991 for FENICE.
DAΦNE was built inside the ADONE building after the 1993 shutdown (INFN-LNF page).

beam_energy.quote: The 1.5 GeV per beam, 105 m long storage ring is divided into 12 equal cells

circumference.note: The page says the ring is 105 m long; recorded as the circumference.
circumference.quote: The 1.5 GeV per beam, 105 m long storage ring is divided into 12 equal cells

cms_energy.note: Design maximum; the INFN-LNF page says the experiments explored collisions 'up to 3.0 GeV in the center of mass'. About 3.1 GeV was reached for the J/psi in November 1974 (see the phase).
cms_energy.quote: ADONE, the electron-positron collider with 3.0 GeV center of mass energy, was envisaged by Bruno Touschek as soon it became clear that AdA would work.

injection_energy.note: The energy of the Varian injector linac.
injection_energy.quote: a 350 MeV Linac, built by Varian (USA), was used as an electron and positron injector

peak_luminosity.note: The page states the design luminosity per crossing was achieved.
peak_luminosity.quote: the achievement of the design luminosity of 3x10^29 cm^-2 s^-1 per crossing

summary.plain: The electron-positron collider at Italy's Frascati laboratory that began colliding beams in 1969, a ring 105 metres around at up to 3 GeV total energy. Its experiments found that electron-positron collisions make hadrons at a high rate and later joined the study of the J/psi. It shut down in 1993.
summary.technical: ADONE: e⁺e⁻ storage ring, 105 m, 1.5 GeV per beam (√s up to 3.0 GeV), 12 cells with four experimental straight sections, Varian 350 MeV injector linac; construction from 1963, first electron beam stored end 1967, colliding-beam physics 1969-1978 (Gamma-Gamma, Mu-Pion, Boson, BCF; then Gamma-Gamma 2, MEA, Baryon-Antibaryon), synchrotron-radiation and gamma-ray source from 1978, FENICE 1990-1993; shut down 26 April 1993; the building then hosted DAΦNE.
